incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager: Sev 2 - fabric heartbeat suppression detected in cluster serve-west-1. Multiple nodes stopped acknowledging IB heartbeats. Auto-escalation to oncall. thread_id=1769876543
Erin (oncall): I'm on it. grabbing logs from the edge rack now. any obvious customer-facing errors?
Ji (support): We're seeing a small spike in 503s for embeddings route from two paying customers — started ~08:11 UTC. Holding customers updated.
Dmitri: seeing repeated driver retransmit logs on host gpu-19-03: "infiniband: heartbeat timeout, probe_count=4". Also the kubelet shows pod restarts on serve-pool-3.
Natalie: attaching quick tail from runtime: ```
2026-01-09T08:11:02Z runtime ERROR kv-cache: put failed: rpc write failed: timeout
2026-01-09T08:11:03Z cuda WARN  out-of-memory trying alloc 256MB
2026-01-09T08:11:04Z infra INFO  network: ib heartbeat miss from 10.10.3.19
```
Priyam: if IB heartbeats drop the KV cache replication will stall and we get OOMs due to retry amplification. Likely root chain: fabric -> kvcache stalls -> backlog -> OOMs.
Erin (oncall): ok mitigation plan: (1) isolate failing hosts, (2) shift traffic to fallback model variant w/ smaller batch & quantized weights, (3) reduce per-host batch_target to avoid queue buildup. I'll coordinate with infra to cordon nodes.
Dmitri: cordon command ready. running: `kubectl cordon gpu-19-03 && kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data gpu-19-03 -l serve=pool-3`
Erin (oncall): executed cordon/drain on gpu-19-03 and gpu-19-04. starting controlled pod restarts on pool-3 to clear stuck KV connections.
incident-bot: Automated action: routed 30% of traffic for route /v1/embeddings to model: redwood/fallback-128q while drain in progress.
Ji (support): customer update sent: "We detected transient network fabric issues causing some request errors; engineering is rerouting and performing node isolation — we'll follow up with post-incident details."
Natalie: logs show immediate drop in retransmits after cordon for the isolated hosts, but host gpu-19-02 still reporting probe misses.
Priyam: for now set runtime config: `batch_target=1` and `kvcache_prefetch=false` on pool-3. That should prevent queue amplification.
Dmitri: applied config change via `redwoodctl deploy-config --cluster serve-west-1 --pool pool-3 --set batch_target=1,kvcache_prefetch=false` — changes rolled to 80% of nodes in pool-3.
Erin (oncall): we also triggered an emergency fallback policy: any pod reporting >3 IB misses will be moved to degraded pool and requests routed to quantized fallback.
sre-bot: Alert: CUDA OOM count dropped from 14/min to 2/min after reroute and batch change.
Ji (support): now seeing 503s drop back to baseline. Customers report degraded latency but functioning.
Natalie: attaching snippet from kernel dmesg on gpu-19-02: ```
[ 12345.678901] mlx5_core 0000:81:00.0: mlx5_cmd: devx create qp failed (-110)
[ 12345.679123] rdma: mlx5: driver reset due to cmd timeout
```
Priyam: that looks like a transient firmware hitch on the IB NIC. Ops has low-level firmware logs in parallel. Recommend scheduling a maintenance window for NIC firmware patch if we see recurrence.
Dmitri: I'm marking nodes gpu-19-02,gpu-19-05 for post-incident hardware triage. Put them in maintenance.
Erin (oncall): handoff: I'm passing to morning shift — summary: fabric heartbeat suppression caused KV cache stalls -> backlog -> some CUDA OOMs and pod restarts. Immediate mitigations executed: node cordon/drain (gpu-19-03/04), traffic routing to quantized fallback, runtime batch_target lowered, kvcache_prefetch disabled. Impact: ~2% requests got 503s during peak; two customers saw errors and were notified. Current status: degraded but stable; OOM rate reduced; two nodes under maintenance.
Ji (support): I'll keep customer comms open and schedule follow-up with account owners.
Erin (oncall): next steps for followup: (a) infra to review NIC firmware and link stats (Dmitri), (b) runtime team to look into kvcache backpressure logic and add graceful degrade (Natalie & Priyam), (c) SRE to add automated rollback if OOMs spike after reroutes.
Dmitri: noted. collecting pcap + ethtool reports and will drop into the postmortem doc. Link: https://redwood.internal/incidents/1769876543/postmortem (placeholder)
Erin (oncall): leaving a short handoff writeup for second-shift: `Handoff: sev2 -> fabric heartbeat suppression; mitigations applied; support notified; monitoring for relapse for next 6h; contact oncall if OOM >5/min or 503% >1%`
incident-bot: Pager cleared at 08:37 UTC after stabilization checks passed.
Erin (oncall): signing off from active. thanks everyone. :white_check_mark:
Priyam: quick note — consider adding a kvcache circuit-breaker to avoid cascade OOMs on replication stalls. filing ticket.
Natalie: saving logs and traces to runbook folder. will attach evals for quantized fallback to ensure quality didn't regress.
Dmitri: done collecting hardware logs. scheduling NIC firmware maintenance for next maintenance window.
Ji (support): final customer follow-up scheduled EOD. closing thread when postmortem complete.
